messages:
Marta G: pager: GPU pool `ca-east-1-gpu` reporting sustained queue growth and 5xx tail errors. autoscaler attempts failing, nodes showing repeated OOMs and CUDA Xid events. escalation to oncall.
SRE-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • severity=high • pager=oncall-sre • alert: gpu_pool_queue_growth (alerts.redwood/infra)
Jonah S: seeing queue length jump ~3.2k over 10m, avg latency >3s. autoscaler logs show 'scale attempt rejected: quota limit' at 4623456940.
Tess P: quick check — capacity report shows 12/24 GPUs reporting "unavailable" due to driver runtime crashes (oom + kernel resets). likely effective capacity ~60%.
Marta G: customer impact: multiple paying tenants report increased 5xx and rate-limited responses, some embeddings jobs failing. flagged CS.
Support Bot: Raised ticket #INC-2987 to account ops, pinged CS for impacted customers list.
Jonah S: logs from one driver node:
```
[4623456994] nvmlDeviceGetComputeRunningProcesses_v3 failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
[4623456995] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79
[4623456996] containerd: oom kill process pid=21401
```
Jonah S: nodes flapping: gpu-node-az1-12 and gpu-node-az1-09 are the worst.
Marta G: initial mitigation plan: 1) temporarily scale down non-prod pools, 2) drain worst nodes, 3) restart gpu-driver-daemonset on drained nodes, 4) open manual capacity request with infra (if autoscaler still blocked).
SRE-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: @oncall accepted. oncall window started 4623457020.
Sidharth K: manual scale-up request to cloud quota team is pending — estimated 45m delay. manual capacity not an immediate option.
Tess P: doing expedited roll of driver on node gpu-node-az1-09: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-az1-09 && kubectl drain gpu-node-az1-09 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
Eng-Runtime: note — rolling driver may cause short reconnects for running jobs, prefer draining then rebooting the driver kernel module and then uncordon.
Jonah S: applied drain and restarted driver container on gpu-node-az1-09. logs show fewer Xid events after restart, node back to Ready but still occasional OOMs.
Marta G: scaled down low-priority batch pools by 40% to free up 6 GPUs — this reduced queue by ~800 in 8m.
Support Bot: CS updated customers: "We are investigating increased latency and job failures; our team is mitigating and will provide ETA shortly." :ear:
Tess P: temporary routing rule applied: route heavy inference routes to fallback model variant (smaller quantized) in us-west while we stabilize ca-east.
Jonah S: autoscaler still rejects new nodes due to policy quota: `QuotaExceeded: gpu-vpc-cores` — working with infra to loosen safety threshold for incident.
Marta G: quick post-mortem notes in thread: probable root = driver/runtime instability cascading into effective capacity loss, autoscaler unable to replenish due to quota and scale-limit config; resulted in sustained queue growth and customer-facing 5xx.
Sidharth K: mitigation summary: driver restarts on 4 nodes, drained 2 flapping nodes, scaled down non-prod pools, applied routing fallback, manual quota request in flight. monitoring shows queue slope flattening.
Jonah S: requesting oncall handoff in 40m to ops-oncall for followup and post-incident cleanup. initiating incident channel and tagging SRE lead for blameless postmortem.
Marta G: noted. please capture exact node IDs and kernel logs for postmortem. I'll update incident ticket with customer impact matrix and timeline.
Eng-Runtime: will push a soft-fix to avoid aggressive eviction in kernel driver on next rolling deployment; will include KV-cache safe restart guidance.
SRE-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE • severity=high -> decreased (monitoring) • next update scheduled in 20m. :white_check_mark:
Marta G: thanks all — continuing monitoring. if queue growth restarts, escalate to oncall-pager immediately. :alert:
